Add a donor's estimated glomerular filtration rate

Source: R/add_donor_egfr.R
add_donor_egfr.Rd

Computes creatinine-based estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR, in mL/min/1.73 m\(^2\)) for donors with a CKD-EPI equation and appends it (default column DON_EGFR).

Usage

add_donor_egfr(
  df,
  equation = c("ckd_epi_2021", "ckd_epi_2009"),
  creatinine = "DON_CREAT",
  adults_only = TRUE,
  egfr_col = "DON_EGFR"
)

Arguments

df

A data frame of donors or transplants, one row each.

equation

"ckd_epi_2021" (default), refit without race, or "ckd_epi_2009", the earlier equation with a race coefficient, for comparison with older work.

creatinine

Name of the creatinine column. Defaults to "DON_CREAT" (deceased donor terminal creatinine). Other choices include "DON_KI_CREAT_PREOP" for living donors, or a peak or final value.

adults_only

If TRUE (default), donors under 18 get a missing value: CKD-EPI was developed in adults.

egfr_col

Name of the output column.

Value

df with a new column.

Details

Input columns: DON_AGE (years), DON_GENDER (F or M), and the serum creatinine column named by creatinine (mg/dL). The 2009 equation also needs DON_RACE_BLACK_AFRICAN_AMERICAN (Y/N), or DON_RACE (16 = Black or African American; 1024 = unknown) when that column is absent. A creatinine that is not a positive number, an unknown sex and, for the 2009 equation, an unknown race give a missing value.

A deceased donor's creatinine is often not at a steady state, so this value describes the creatinine more than the kidney's filtration rate.

References

Inker LA, Eneanya ND, Coresh J, et al. New creatinine- and cystatin C-based equations to estimate GFR without race. N Engl J Med 2021;385:1737-1749. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2102953 (Table 2, which gives both the 2021 equation and the 2009 equation.)

Levey AS, Stevens LA, Schmid CH, et al. A new equation to estimate glomerular filtration rate. Ann Intern Med 2009;150:604-612. doi:10.7326/0003-4819-150-9-200905050-00006

See also

Guides:

  • The scores

  • Missing and unknown inputs

Examples

donors <- data.frame(
  DON_AGE = c(50, 30),
  DON_GENDER = c("F", "M"),
  DON_CREAT = c(0.6, 2.0)
)
add_donor_egfr(donors)
#>   DON_AGE DON_GENDER DON_CREAT  DON_EGFR
#> 1      50          F       0.6 109.28301
#> 2      30          M       2.0  45.19737
